symbol_mode_info: Choose how symbols represent your data: fixed size, proportional to a value, grouped into classes, or by category.
proportional_type_info: Single: one symbol per feature. Double: two half-symbols to compare two values.
size_according_info: Select the numeric variable that determines each symbol's size.
max_size_info: Maximum size in pixels for the largest value. Smaller values are scaled proportionally.
shape_info: Geometric shape used to represent each feature on the map.
show_missing_data_info: Display a specific symbol for features with no data, so they remain visible on the map.
fill_section_info: Interior color of the symbols. Can be fixed, vary by class, or by category.
stroke_section_info: Outline drawn around each symbol. Helps distinguish overlapping features.
unique_size_info: Fixed size in pixels applied to all symbols.
category_variable_info: Select the variable whose distinct values define the color categories.
symbols_section_info: Symbols represent point features on the map (points, circles, squares, etc.). Configure their size, shape, color, and opacity.
polygons_section_info: Polygons represent area features on the map (regions, countries, parcels, etc.). Configure their fill and stroke.
lines_section_info: Lines represent linear features on the map (roads, borders, flows, etc.). Configure their thickness, color, and style.
labels_section_info: Labels display text associated with each map feature, such as a name or value.
texts_section_info: Texts allow adding free annotations on the map, independently of geographic features.
labels_disabled_no_geometry: Labels require geographic data (points, lines or polygons)
texts_disabled_no_geometry: Texts require geographic data (points, lines or polygons)
data_visualized_info: Select the data column to display on the map. Suggestions adapt to the type of variable chosen.
basemap_style_info: Tiled basemap style: desaturated to avoid interfering with data, simple for a neutral look, or aerial for a satellite view.
map_projection_info: Mercator: classic flat projection. Globe: 3D spherical representation, useful for worldwide data.
basemap_tiled_info: Enables a tiled basemap (OpenStreetMap) instead of vector layers. Useful for geographic context but hides customizable layers.
geo_step_info: Georeferencing locates your data on the map by associating it with known geographic features or GPS coordinates.
geo_reference_info: Entities: match your data to place names (countries, regions, cities). Coordinates: use latitude/longitude columns.
geo_linked_variable_info: Column in your data that contains geographic identifiers (country names, ISO codes, region names, etc.).
geo_longitude_info: Column containing longitude values (East-West coordinate, between -180 and 180).
geo_latitude_info: Column containing latitude values (North-South coordinate, between -90 and 90).
basemap_step_info: The basemap provides geographic outlines (countries, regions, etc.) on which your data is projected. The join links your data to the basemap.
join_assisted_info: The assisted join automatically compares values in your geographic column with basemap features and flags uncertain matches.
enrich_step_info: Enrich your dataset by joining an external tabular file or overlaying an additional basemap.
